text:
maya: Acme is hitting 502s on hosted inference when uploading ~40MB payloads. Started ~10:12 PST. They say the request fails at the edge with 'upstream prematurely closed connection' and include edge trace id tr-9f7a3.

sanjay: Can you paste the full request headers + the edge trace? suspecting Authorization header gets truncated somewhere in frontdoor -> envoy path.

maya: Customer supplied the curl they used and a short excerpt from their network capture: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -F 'input=@large.json' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer
> POST /v1/infer HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...<redacted>
> Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary
> Content-Length: 42103456
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< x-edge-trace: tr-9f7a3
< 
{"error":"upstream prematurely closed connection"}
```
They also gave the host upstream id up-0def456.

oliver: Noted. We saw a similar symptom last month where large multipart bodies + many headers triggered a buffer/connwindow interaction in ingress. Could be NGINX proxy_buffer_size or Envoy h2 window exhaustion.

dana: I'm pulling logs for tr-9f7a3 now. Quick grep shows repeated auth header "Authorization: Bearer <truncated>" on the edge, and upstream upstream_response_time ~0.00. Looks like upstream process never got the full header. Attaching short snippet: 
```
edge-log 1751234000 tr-9f7a3 recv_headers: len=827
edge-log 1751234001 tr-9f7a3 forward_to_envoy: headers_len=827
envoy 1751234002 tr-9f7a3 envoy_recv: header_bytes=512 envoy_buf_truncate=true
upstream 1751234003 up-0def456 conn_close reason=client_closed
```
This suggests header bytes clipped at 512 boundary before full Authorization reached upstream.

angelica: Customer is blocked on a demo today. Short-term workaround: ask them to switch to chunked upload (split file) or use the multipart chunking in our SDK. Also possible to set X-Use-Chunked: true as a temporary header.

sanjay: For a durable fix, two action items: 1) verify nginx/envoy header buffer and large header settings across frontdoor pool, 2) add a temporary heuristic at edge to reject instead of silently truncating when header_len > threshold (return 431 instead of forwarding truncated header).

maya: Repro steps I validated locally against staging: 
1) create a 40MB JSON blob (python -c "open('big.json','wb').write(b'x'*42000000)")
2) curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $(printf "A%.0s" {1..800})' -F 'input=@big.json' https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/infer
Result: staging returns 502 with edge trace st-3b2a1 and logs show envoy_buf_truncate=true.

dana: I'm going to open a prioritised infra ticket with eng-infra and eng-runtime. Tentative title: "edge: header truncation on large multipart requests causing 502 to upstream". Will include traces tr-9f7a3 / st-3b2a1, log snippets, and the curl repro.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1145 assigned to eng-infra, priority P1, link: https://internal.redwood.incidents/INC-2026-1145

oliver: Quick mitigation we can try now: bump envoy buffer limit in the canary frontdoor pool from 512 -> 2048 and recycle pods in the canary region. If that reduces errors we can roll global. I can push a canary change in the next 10-15m.

angelica: Please coordinate with me before rolling — I'll message Acme with the workaround + ETA to avoid duplicate steps.

maya: Thanks. Dana, assign INC and add affected customer tag (acme-demo). We'll keep this thread for updates.

dana: Done. INC-2026-1145 updated, linked traces and repro. Next: oliver to push canary, eng-infra to monitor 502 rate for tenant-tag=acme-demo and global streaming 502s.

oliver: Canary started (rolling 3/5 pods) -> will report in 10m.

maya: Noted. I'll tell Acme to try chunked upload in the meantime and share the trace ids so we can correlate. :thumbsup:
